claims.question: q1
claims.claim: 73% of respondents use coding assistants and agents daily, and nearly a third of daily users spend upwards of four hours per day using them.
claims.quote: The overwhelming majority of respondents now use coding assistants and agents daily (73%), with nearly a third of daily users spending upwards of four hours.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: AI is seeing meaningful adoption in secondary review functions, including analyzing telemetry, reviewing pull requests, and hunting for security issues.
claims.quote: Even secondary review functions—analyzing telemetry, reviewing pull requests, hunting for security issues—are seeing meaningful AI adoption.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: 48% of respondents trust AI when they can easily validate the answers, while only 16% extend that trust to most tasks that are not important work decisions.
claims.quote: When asked when it’s acceptable to trust AI, 48% indicate they trust AI when they can easily validate the answers and only 16% extend that trust to most tasks that are not important work decisions.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Human-in-the-loop is the dominant mode of working with AI tools.
claims.quote: That’s why human-in-the-loop is the dominant mode of working with these tools.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Six out of ten users cite a reason to avoid using AI at work or school, and losing job skills is a top concern.
claims.quote: 6 out of 10 users cite a reason to avoid using AI at work or school, losing job skills is a top concern.

claims.question: q5
